parties: Polycab India Limited (captive user) | Continuum Green Energy Limited (renewable energy supplier)
headline: Polycab enters group captive arrangement with Continuum Green Energy for renewable power at Jamnagar facility
sum: Polycab India has entered into a group captive arrangement for procurement of renewable power from Continuum Green Energy Limited for its manufacturing facility in Jamnagar, Gujarat. The transaction involved equity investment by Polycab in Continuum and execution of Power Consumption Agreement and Share Purchase and Shareholders Agreement.
implication: Group captive structures leveraging the Electricity (Amendment) Rules 2026 framework (effective 13 March 2026) offer C&I consumers statutory clarity on proportionality, ESS-mediated consumption, and intra-state nodal verification, materially improving project bankability and reducing regulatory litigation risk in green power procurement.
detail: Polycab acquired equity in Continuum Green Energy to establish a group captive power arrangement for its Jamnagar manufacturing facility. The transaction structure involved negotiation of a Power Consumption Agreement and Share Purchase and Shareholders Agreement. This deal reflects the evolving C&I sector strategy toward renewable energy captive procurement and aligns with Electricity (Amendment) Rules 2026, which codify the 26% ownership / 51% consumption thresholds and establish a statutory two-tier captive status verification mechanism (state nodal agency for intra-state; NLDC for inter-state arrangements). Continuum supplies electricity to over 180 C&I consumers with a 4.7 GWp renewable portfolio (approximately 2.4 GWp operational as of announcement), and recently secured ₹1,350 crore from Chubu Electric Power Co., reinforcing its scale and institutional investor backing.

framework.note: Core statutory foundation for captive generating plants; permits consumers to establish and operate CGPs for their own consumption and benefit from open access exemptions (CSS/AS waivers).

framework.ref: Electricity Rules, 2005 (Rule 3, as amended by Electricity (Amendment) Rules, 2026 effective 13 March 2026)
framework.note: Dual-condition framework: (i) captive users collectively hold ≥26% ownership in CGP; (ii) ≥51% of aggregate annual electricity consumed for captive use. For AoP structures, proportionality principle (1.96x ratio, ±10% variance) applies per ownership share; new rules cap individual consumption at 100% of proportionate entitlement (110% if holding ≥26% ownership individually). Ownership now includes direct or indirect equity through holding company, subsidiaries, or subsidiary of holding company.

framework.ref: Electricity (Amendment) Rules, 2026 (Rule 3(4), effective 1 April 2026) - Verification Framework
framework.note: Establishes statutory two-tier verification: intra-state captive status verified by State-designated Nodal Agency; inter-state arrangements fall under NLDC per Central Government approval. Appeals before Grievance Redressal Committee. Pending verification, CSS/AS not levied if captive user furnishes prescribed declaration.

framework.ref: Electricity (Amendment) Rules, 2026 (Rule 3(1)(a)) - Energy Storage System (ESS) Consumption
framework.note: Expressly recognizes electricity consumed through ESS connected to a CGP as valid captive consumption, enabling hybrid solar-plus-storage and wind-plus-storage configurations and removal of regulatory ambiguity on battery-mediated captive use.

framework.ref: Electricity Rules, 2005 (Rule 3(2)) - Definition of Captive User
framework.note: Expanded by 2026 amendments to include consumption by subsidiary company (Companies Act 2013 s.2(87)) and holding company (s.2(46)) of the captive user, treating group entities as a single captive user for consumption calculation purposes.

framework.ref: Competition Commission of India (CCI) - FDI / Sectoral Clearance
framework.note: Relevant if Continuum's equity dilution via Polycab stake triggers CCI notification threshold under M&A rules (typically ≥₹1,000 cr asset value or ≥40% market share in relevant market); parallel Chubu Electric Power investment (₹1,350 cr) in Continuum subject to CCI approval as reported.

framework.ref: Ministry of Power Notification - Renewable Energy / Clean Energy Initiatives
framework.note: Aligns with National Electricity Policy 2005 recognition of captive generation as enabling reliable, cost-effective industrial power supply; supports India's 500 GW renewable target by 2030 and industrial energy transition.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015 (Reg. 30)
framework.note: If Polycab India (NSE: POLYCAB, BSE: 542652) classifies this equity investment as a material transaction or related party transaction, disclosure to stock exchanges required under Reg. 30 or Reg. 23(9) (Related Party Transactions).

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Renewable Energy Investments & Deductions
framework.note: Potential tax incentives for renewable energy generation / investment under Section 80-IA (deduction for newly established industrial undertakings in specified sectors) or accelerated depreciation under Schedule II; relevant to economic modeling of Polycab's captive procurement.

structure.consideration: Equity stake in Continuum Green Energy Limited for renewable power procurement arrangement; specific investment amount and equity percentage not disclosed in primary source or corroborating announcements.
conditions: Execution of Power Consumption Agreement (PCA) between Polycab and Continuum, specifying power to be procured, pricing, duration, and take-or-pay terms
Execution of Share Purchase Agreement and Shareholders Agreement governing Polycab's equity investment in Continuum and governance/board representation rights

Compliance with Electricity Act 2003 Section 9 and Electricity Rules 2005 Rule 3 requirements for group captive status: (i) collective ≥26% ownership by captive users (Polycab and any co-investors); (ii) ≥51% annual consumption for captive use
Compliance with Electricity (Amendment) Rules 2026 proportionality and consumption cap regime (100% of proportionate entitlement per ownership share, or 110% if ≥26% individual ownership)
Registration / verification of captive status with relevant State Nodal Agency (Gujarat, for Jamnagar intra-state arrangement) per Rule 3(4) Electricity (Amendment) Rules 2026, effective 1 April 2026
Parallel regulatory approvals for Continuum's fundraising (e.g., CCI approval for Chubu Electric Power investment, which may impact Continuum's cap table and Polycab's ownership %)
Completion of due diligence on Continuum's operational and under-construction renewable capacity to ensure ≥51% of generation available for captive consumption by Polycab and co-investors
approvals: Continuum Green Energy board / shareholder approval (internal)
State Nodal Agency (Gujarat) verification of captive status under Rule 3(4) Electricity (Amendment) Rules 2026
Potential CCI notification / review if material share of Continuum acquired and cross-shareholding / investment gating thresholds triggered
SEBI disclosure / approval if Polycab India classifies as material related party transaction (if Continuum promoters or Chubu Electric Power are related to Polycab)
structure.novel: Application of Electricity (Amendment) Rules 2026 (effective 13 March 2026) framework in a marquee industrial captive arrangement: the new statutory two-tier verification mechanism (state nodal agency for intra-state; NLDC for inter-state), proportionality cap at 100% (110% for ≥26% individual ownership holder), and formal recognition of ESS-mediated consumption eliminate prior judicial ambiguity and reduce regulatory litigation risk, enabling C&I consumers to structure long-term renewable PPAs with bankable certainty. Polycab's investment in Continuum reflects the transition from traditional open-access procurement to equity-based group captive models in the post-2026 amendments environment.
